name: World Literature Minor
faculty: Faculty of Arts and Social Sciences

sections.title: Lower Division Requirements

requirements.title: Check with an advisor
requirements.text: Students complete a total of 12 units.

sections.note:
Students complete a total of 12 units, including.
one 100-level WL Writing course
*Students may count one 2nd year language course (3 units) toward their lower division WL units.

requirements.title: Check with an advisor
requirements.text: Students complete a minimum total of 16 upper division units in WL courses, of which at least four must be taken at the 400-level.

requirements.title: Check with an advisor
requirements.text: With prior approval, students may complete one lower or upper division relevant topic course (up to four units) from outside the World Literature Program by submitting the course description to the World Literature advisor.

grades.label: Grade Requirements
grades.text: In addition to the normal university degree requirements, students must obtain a minimum 2.00 WL cumulative grade point average (CGPA) (calculated on all WL courses completed at SFU), and a minimum 2.00 WL CUDGPA (calculated on all upper division WL courses completed at SFU).

grades.label: Faculty of Arts and Social Sciences Degree Requirements
grades.text: For all bachelor of arts (BA) programs, students complete 120 units, which includes at least 60 units that must be completed at Simon Fraser University at least 45 upper division units, of which at least 30 upper division units must be completed at Simon Fraser University at least 60 units (including 21 upper division units) in Faculty of Arts and Social Sciences courses satisfaction of the writing, quantitative, and breadth requirements an overall cumulative grade point average (CGPA) and upper division overall CGPA of at least 2.0, and program CGPA and upper division program CGPA of at least 2.0 on the course work used to satisfy the minimum program requirements.

grades.label: Faculty of Arts and Social Sciences Degree Requirements
grades.text: FASS departments may define additional GPA requirements for their respective programs.
